EDAX Pattern Viewer:
This tab is designed to let you quickly load, visualize, and interact with EDAX .up1 binary pattern files and their associated .edaxh5 map metadata. It allows you to probe patterns directly from a generated map and set Regions of Interest (ROI) for downstream processing.

• Load .edaxh5: Extracts grid dimensions (Nx, Ny) and metadata crucial for scaling and orientation.
• Load .up1: Loads the binary diffraction pattern file into memory.
• Initialize Interactive Map: Loads the dataset into fast memory (RAM) and draws the interactive 2D spatial map.
• Map Field: Switch the displayed map layer to view different extracted fields like IQ, CI, Phase, or SEM Signal.
• Pattern Colormap: Change the color palette applied to the Live Pattern Viewer.

Interaction Shortcuts:
- Left-Click & Drag on the Map: Actively probes the grid and displays the exact corresponding diffraction pattern on the right.
- Shift + Left-Click & Drag: Draw a rectangular Region of Interest (ROI). This mask will be used by the NML Builder to limit the indexing boundaries.
EDAX NML Builder:
This tab generates the .nml configuration file that is required by the EMSphInx application to perform spherical indexing. You define your physical detector boundaries, structure information, and advanced spherical indexing parameters here before sending the job to the queue.

• Find/Fetch SHT from GitHub API: Queries the EMsoft SHT Database for a Master Pattern matching your Element, Structure, and kV inputs. It will automatically check your local SHT_Library first before downloading.
• Browse: Allows you to manually load local .sht files into your library and format their names correctly.
• Remove: Deletes selected Master Patterns from the job's execution list.
• Generate NML & Add to Queue: Writes out the parameter .nml file and automatically queues it for WSL execution in Tab 3.

Parameter Details:
- Bandwidth: Controls the spherical harmonic resolution. Higher bandwidths provide more accuracy but run slower (Common values: 123, 158, 188).
- Apply Gaussian Background: Enables a high-pass image filter on the patterns to remove gradients.
- NRegions: Controls the size of the high-pass filter grid (10 is generally a good default).
- Threads: The number of logical CPU cores to dedicate to this task (0 uses all available).
Oxford Map Viewer:
This tab allows you to inspect Oxford .h5oina pattern files. Unlike the EDAX format, Oxford consolidates both the map metadata and raw binary patterns within a single H5 file. This interface lets you extract the map geometry, visualize different field modalities, and draw Regions of Interest (ROI) before indexing.

• Load .h5oina: Reads the file and extracts all available scans, grid dimensions (Nx, Ny), and maps.
• Select Map from H5: Choose which specific scanning region inside the file you want to analyze.
• Select Patterns: Choose between 'Processed Patterns' (typically background corrected) or 'Unprocessed Patterns' to display.
• Initialize Interactive Map: Loads the map data and populates the viewer pane.
• Display Settings: Switch between extracted map types (such as Band Contrast) and toggle Pattern Colormaps.

Interaction Shortcuts:
- Left-Click & Drag on the Map: Probes the map grid and displays the corresponding diffraction pattern on the right.
- Shift + Left-Click & Drag: Draw a rectangular Region of Interest (ROI). This limits indexing boundaries in the NML Builder.
Oxford NML Builder:
The Oxford NML Builder generates both the EMSphInx .nml configuration file and simultaneously converts the embedded patterns from your .h5oina file into a compatible .up1 binary file format. This process happens asynchronously in the background so you can continue queuing additional jobs without waiting.

• Find/Fetch SHT from GitHub API: Queries the EMsoft database for Master Patterns matching your parameters. It checks your local library first.
• Browse / Remove: Add local files to your library or remove them from the current job.
• Create NML and up1 & add to job queue: Immediately writes the NML file and pushes the UP1 conversion task to the Job Queue background processor.

Workflow Details:
- UP1 Generation: Oxford patterns are tightly packed inside the H5 file. The Job Queue will safely unpack them into a new .up1 file in blocks. Multiple jobs referencing the same UP1 will intelligently wait for the unpacker to finish.
- Region of Interest (ROI): Restricting the indexing bounds will apply to the generated NML file (it does not crop the UP1 file itself).
- Memory Considerations: If your H5 file is extremely large, the unpacker will batch the write operations to avoid filling up your RAM.
Job Queue:
The Job Queue is the command center for executing your configured NML jobs using the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL). It runs processes asynchronously, providing real-time output from EMSphInx without freezing the studio interface.

• Start Queue: Begins sequential execution of all 'Pending' jobs in the list.
• Stop: Safely sends a kill signal to the currently running process and pauses the queue.
• Load Existing NML: Ingests an already created .nml file directly into the queue. It validates that all referenced files exist locally.
• Remove Selected / Clear Finished: Cleans up the queue list.

Advanced Features:
- Auto-Mounting: If your data is located on a mapped network drive (e.g., N:), the queue will automatically ensure the share is mounted in WSL via drvfs. If the password is required, it will prompt you securely and save it for future automated mounting.
- Live Output Console: Streams terminal output directly from the EMSphInx indexer, parsed efficiently to ensure the interface remains highly responsive.
